pahārāda.notes: AN 8.19 gives the conversation at Verañjā. The occurrence at the end of AN 8.20 is the chapter’s verse listing the discourses.

pahāsa.notes: SN 42.2:2.11 explicitly names the hell (pahāso nāma nirayo). Sujato translates the name as ‘Laughter’, so the packet misses it. The citation lands in SN 42.1.

pajjota.notes: MN 108:2.1 names the king whom Ajātasattu fears. The candidate describes a tank built by Duṭṭhagāmaṇī in the Mahāvaṁsa. MN 51 supplies no evidence for that tank. A dictionary entry for the king is missing here.

pajjunna.notes: DPPN explicitly includes the DN 32 guardian in its account of the rain god. DN 20 describes his thundering arrival, and SN 1.39–40 name his daughters. SN 1.38 is a neighboring discourse.

palāsavana.notes: MN 68 and AN 10.67–68 place the grove at Naḷakapāna. The page references also pick up MN 67 and AN 10.66.

panāda.notes: DN 20 and DN 32 list Panāda alongside Opamañña. Thag 2.22:1.1 explicitly calls its Panāda a king. The packet has no entry for him.

pasenadi.notes: AN 5.49 names Pasenadi at Mallikā’s death. AN 5.50 concerns King Muṇḍa. AN 5.30–31 and SN 6.10–12 also lack a named mention of Pasenadi. The chamberlains’ account of riding with his wives is in SN 55.6.

pañcakaṅga.notes: The discussion with Udāyī is in MN 59 and SN 36.19. Pañcakaṅga also invites Anuruddha to his house in MN 127. The citations pick up the neighboring MN 58, SN 36.18, and MN 126.

pañcasikha.notes: The report of the gods’ assembly is in DN 19. DPPN’s DN.i.220 lands in DN 11. DN 21:1.6.5 dates the love song to shortly after the Buddha’s awakening, while the entry dates it before. The name also occurs in the closing summary at SN 35.123:2.3.

pañcasālā.notes: The almsround in the Magadhan brahmin village is in SN 4.18. SN 4.17 is an adjacent text.

pañcālacaṇḍa.notes: SN 2.7 calls the speaker a devaputta, and AN 9.42 quotes his verse. DN 32:10.16 lists a guardian of this name. DPPN makes their identity conjectural, and DN 32 gives no detail that connects the guardian to the verse. SN 2.5, 2.6, and 2.8 concern other speakers. SN 2.10 mentions him in the chapter summary.

paṇḍara.notes: Thag 17.1:1.3 identifies Phussa’s questioner by his clan in the compound paṇḍarasagotto. This accounts for the DPPN entry, while the DPD sense describes a type of elephant.

paṇḍitakumāraka.notes: AN 3.74 names both Licchavis visiting Ānanda. The DPD hint points to AN 3.75 and the page citation also picks up AN 3.73.

paṭācārā.notes: AN 1.238 names her foremost in monastic law. The adjacent AN 1.219–234 and 1.248–257 ranges concern other disciples. Her own Thig 5.10 describes washing her feet and extinguishing a lamp. The verses about losing husband, children, parents, and brother occur in Thig 10.1 under Kisāgotamī.

pessa.notes: MN 51:1.3 calls Pessa the elephant marshal’s son (hatthārohaputto). He describes his own experience training elephants at MN 51:4.13.

phagguna.notes: DPD specifies Moḷiyaphagguna in MN 21. SN 12.12:7.1 also addresses him as Phagguna, and SN 12.32 reports that he left the training. SN 35.83 calls its questioner simply Phagguna. DPPN tentatively connects him to the sick monk of AN 6.56. Neither passage identifies him as Moḷiyaphagguna. AN 6.56:8.2–3 states release from the five lower fetters, whereas the entry claims arahantship. AN 6.55 and SN 35.81–82 are neighboring citations.

phalagaṇḍa.notes: SN 1.50:3.1 and SN 2.24:4.1 list him second among the seven monks reborn in Aviha. Both read palagaṇḍo, with its own DPD sense palagaṇḍa 2. The spelling explains the empty mention list. SN 1.49 concerns miserliness.

pilakkhaguhā.notes: Sandaka stays at the cave near Kosambī in MN 76. MN 75 is an adjacent citation.

pilindavaccha.notes: The foremost declaration is AN 1.215. AN 1.198–208 and 1.219–234 concern other disciples. Ud 3.6:4.4 gives five hundred consecutive brahmin births to explain his form of address. DPPN gives one hundred.

pilotika.notes: MN 27:2.2–5 names Pilotika and has Jāṇussoṇi address him as Vacchāyana. MN 26 is an adjacent citation.

piyadassī.notes: MN 116:4.6 explicitly identifies Piyadassī as a paccekasambuddha who lived on Isigili. The other DPD sense refers to a Buddha in the Buddhavaṁsa.

piyaka.notes: AN 5.50 names Muṇḍa’s treasurer and describes his visit to Nārada. AN 5.49 concerns Pasenadi and Mallikā.

piṅgalakoccha.notes: MN 30:2.1 explicitly names the brahmin in both languages. The English spells Piṅgalakoccha as one word with a lowercase k. The packet’s English name filter derives an internal capital K from the DPPN heading and misses the exchange.

piṅgiya.notes: Snp 5.1 and 5.18 list Piṅgiya among the brahmin students who question the Buddha. Snp 5.17 gives the elderly Piṅgiya’s question and Snp 5.19 his account of the Buddha. SN 1.50:3.4 (siṅgiyo) and SN 2.24:4.4 (saṅgiyo) both have Piṅgiya in the English list of seven freed monks in Aviha. Those two suttas are missing from the packet’s permitted IDs. SN 1.49 is a neighboring citation. DPPN’s proposed identity between the two figures remains conjectural.

piṅgiyānī.notes: AN 5.194–195 name the brahmin of Vesālī. The feminine DPD headword describes a Jātaka queen. The tapped forms also give the masculine DPD headword piṅgiyāni, which is missing from this packet’s senses and fits the entry. AN 5.193 concerns Saṅgārava. AN 5.200:7.2 repeats the brahmin’s name in a closing summary.

piṇḍola.notes: MN 116:4.8 names the paccekabuddha. The monk in the DPD hint SN 35.127 is Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja, whose entry is under the compound headword. The short form piṇḍolo referring to the monk also occurs in the summaries at Thag 2.10:3.1, SN 48.50:12.4, and Ud 4.10:5.3.

piṇḍolabhāradvāja.notes: AN 1.195 names the foremost lion-roarer, and SN 35.127 gives the conversation with Udena. AN 1.170–187, AN 1.198–208, and SN 35.125–126 are neighboring citations. DPPN reverses the speaker in Ud 4.6:3.1, where the Buddha speaks after seeing Piṇḍola meditating.

pokkharaṇiyā.notes: AN 6.21:1.1 locates the Buddha at pokkharaṇiyāyaṁ in Sāmagāma. Sujato translates this as a lotus pond. The monastery designation in DPD and DPPN comes from the commentary.

posāla.notes: The citation list captures Snp 5.1, which names him among Bāvarī’s students. The questions and answers that DPPN also cites in verses 1112–1115 are in Snp 5.15.
